checks.finding: design.md's '## Architecture' section (lines 45-120) satisfies all three required elements. (1) Top-level component boundaries: a mermaid flowchart names every new/existing component (PC/PB content files, SCHEMA_PC/SCHEMA_PB, CANON, GEN, STAGE, REG, ANCHOR, DETECT, VALIDATE, PUBLISHER, GUARD, GINV, HANDSHAKE, AGENT, ENTRYPOINTS) with labeled edges describing each boundary's interaction (e.g. 'CANON -->|canonical hash| SIDE_PC', 'GUARD -->|full write-deny, no sudo bypass, 4-basename x 12-call-site matrix| SIDE_PC'). (2) Integration with existing components: GUARD is explicitly labeled 'sdd-hook-guard.py ... (EXISTING, unchanged decision logic)'; GINV is 'guard-invariants.json + generate-guard-invariants.py + generated/* (REQ-007, human-copy edit via PUBLISHER)'; SHIP/BOOT/INTERVIEWER/LITESPEC/LITEGATE map to five existing SKILL.md files listed in the Components table as 'existing, edited'/'existing, human-applied'. (3) Technology choices per layer: the Components table (lines 124-158) has an explicit 'Technology' column for every row (Python, POSIX sh/PowerShell/Node.js, JSON Schema, YAML, JSON, Markdown), and frontend-spec.md's Technology Stack table restates the same choices with rationale/constraint columns. This is a multi-paragraph, multi-edge description, not a one-sentence component-naming summary.

An explicit component dependency graph is present (Architecture mermaid diagram + Components table), so this was checked directly rather than SKIPped. Tracing edges: DETECT depends on ANCHOR ('ANCHOR -.->|default-resolved trust anchor| DETECT'); ANCHOR is produced by PUBLISHER ('PUBLISHER -.->|publishes in lockstep with the sidecar| ANCHOR'); PUBLISHER depends on VALIDATE ('VALIDATE -->|staged candidate PASSES| PUBLISHER'); VALIDATE depends on STAGE ('STAGE -.->|pre-publish validation| VALIDATE'); STAGE is produced by GEN ('GEN -->|...| STAGE'); and GEN depends on DETECT ('DETECT -->|verdict, recomputed fresh, never trusted from a file| GEN'). This closes a directed cycle: GEN -> STAGE -> VALIDATE -> PUBLISHER -> ANCHOR -> DETECT -> GEN. However, this is not a structural/instantiation circular dependency of the kind this check targets (e.g. two modules mutually importing each other, creating ambiguous build/initialization order). Each edge represents a separate, sequential CLI-tool invocation at a distinct point in time within an approval lifecycle (generate -> stage -> validate -> publish -> anchor advances -> a LATER detect/generate cycle re-reads the new anchor); design.md explicitly documents that every step re-derives its inputs fresh rather than caching or assuming simultaneous mutual state ('DETECT ... never trusted from a file', 'Generator/validator never trust an externally-supplied verdict, and never re-derive from a caller-suppliable anchor', requirements.md REQ-006). There is no ambiguous initialization order, no simultaneous mutual instantiation, and no concrete implementation/verification failure mode identified from this loop -- it is the intended, documented shape of a rolling-trust-anchor approval workflow (analogous to a CI pipeline whose output becomes a later run's cached input, not a circular-import defect). No structural cycle defect found.
